purpose: Review an accessible primary fish study that names freshwater, brackish and marine sampling areas along the Lower Agusan River to Butuan Bay, while keeping its historical station-level evidence separate from current presence, natural-diet guidance, safety alerts and app-ready geometry.

studySource.title: Levels of Heavy Metals in Fish and Sediments from Different Salinity Gradients of Lower Agusan River to Butuan Bay, Caraga, Philippines

accessAndReuse.visualReview: Publisher-hosted PDF pages 89-91 visually checked, including Figure 1, Table 1 and the station descriptions.
accessAndReuse.journalPolicyStatement: The journal describes itself as open access and says users may read, download, copy, distribute, print, search or link to article full texts.
accessAndReuse.licenseAssessment: The checked policy and article do not identify a Creative Commons license/version or separately state rights for republishing a table, figure, or derived app content.
accessAndReuse.decision: Keep as a linked research citation and limited attributed summary. Do not copy the PDF/table/figure or publish species, derived content, or records in the app until item-specific reuse is reviewed.

methods.design: Fish were collected across three stations selected along a measured salinity gradient from the Lower Agusan River toward Butuan Bay.
methods.sampleSize: Three species were collected in triplicate at each station; the paper reports three adult-size-range fish per species (27 fish samples across nine table taxa).
methods.identificationAndVoucherStatus: The reviewed article pages provide species labels and collection methods but no collection institution, accession, or specimen-voucher crosswalk was located.
methods.mapNote: Figure 1 depicts three sampling points within each salinity station; the paper text gives one coordinate string per station. Do not derive nine point coordinates or assign the published station coordinate to individual specimens.

stations.locality: Downstream of Barangay Buhangin, Butuan City, Agusan del Norte
Barangay Pagatpatan, Butuan City, Agusan del Norte
Barangay Dahekan, Magallanes, Agusan del Norte

interpretation.evidenceClass: Historical direct-sampling study, not current monitoring.
interpretation.sourceClaim: The authors describe the listed fishes as resident species in the area and classify their trophic levels for the sampling period.
interpretation.naturalDiet: The trophic labels are not stomach-content or natural-prey findings. They do not support the Bangwit 'Ano ang kinakain?' detail or bait recommendations.
interpretation.presence: Taxon-to-station associations are retained only as the paper's 2018 sampling report. They are not imported as present-day range or occurrence assertions.
interpretation.coordinates: Station coordinates are preserved verbatim for provenance only. The article does not state a datum, positional uncertainty, or specimen-level point crosswalk; no coordinate or geometry is admitted.
interpretation.safety: The article measures metals in fish muscles and sediments from 2018. These historical results are not a current advisory, current water-quality assessment, or basis for a present-day consumption warning.
interpretation.denominator: Nine source table taxa are not a complete checklist for the river, bay, city, municipality, or region.

limitations: Sampling took place in April-May 2018 and cannot establish current occupancy or abundance.
The paper provides one coordinate string per station while Figure 1 shows multiple sample points; datum and positional uncertainty were not located.
No voucher accession or collection repository mapping was located in the reviewed article pages, so the field identifications have not been independently checked.
Source table spellings are recorded verbatim pending an independent taxonomic-name cross-check; OCR and secondary abstract text contain spelling variants.
The journal-wide open-access statement does not by itself establish the exact license/version or Bangwit permission for republishing derived records or copied content.
Historical metal measurements are not current safety information, and the study is not a complete fish inventory.
nextAction: Cross-check all nine source table names against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes or another current taxonomic authority. Keep that nomenclatural check separate from specimen identity, local presence, diet and geometry; then perform a bounded independent voucher search only if names and locality spellings are stable.

references.supports: Primary article: sampling period, station descriptions, coordinate strings, salinity values, Figure 1, Table 1 taxa/trophic labels, gears and sample design.
Alternate publisher-hosted copy and abstract spelling cross-check; the table reviewed in the primary PDF remains the transcription source.
Journal-level open-access statement; checked policy does not name a Creative Commons license/version.
